facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The construction of the Karni Mata Temple was concluded in the early 20th century by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner. The entire temple structure is raised in marble and its architecture evinces resemblance to the Mughal style.
facts.text: The present marble structure of the Karni Mata Temple at Deshnoke was completed in the early twentieth century under the patronage of Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner, incorporating late Rajput and Mughal architectural motifs.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The idol of Karni Mata of Bikaner sits within the inner sanctum of the temple,a 75 cm tall statue holding a trident (trishul) in one hand, adorned by a crown and garlands.
facts.text: The inner sanctum of the Deshnoke shrine houses a 0.75-metre-tall stone idol of Karni Mata holding a trident, flanked on either side by images of her sisters.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Adding to the charm of the attractive marble façade are solid silver doors that lead to an entry to the compound within. The panels of the silver doors depict the many legends of the Goddess.
facts.text: The entrance to the temple compound is fitted with solid silver gates featuring relief carvings that depict scenes from the life and legends of Karni Mata.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Out of all the rats, white rats are held specifically sacred as they are believed to be the incarnations of Karni Mata and her sons.
facts.text: Local Charan belief maintains that an estimated 25,000 black rats residing in the Deshnoke sanctuary are holy ancestors known as kaba rather than ordinary pests.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Out of all the rats, white rats are held specifically sacred as they are believed to be the incarnations of Karni Mata and her sons. Visitors put in enormous efforts to draw them out often through offering of sweets.
facts.text: Devotees believe that spotting a rare white rat among the thousands of dark rodents brings exceptional fortune and serves as a direct divine blessing.
